proofs.proof_tex:
Let \(M=U\Sigma V^\top\) be a compact singular-value decomposition, where \(U\in\mathbb R^{N_0\times r}\) and \(V\in\mathbb R^{T_0\times r}\) have orthonormal columns and \(\Sigma=\operatorname{diag}(\sigma_1,\ldots,\sigma_r)\).  Assumptions~\ref{ass:exact-rank} and~\ref{ass:singular-gap} give \(\sigma_r\ge\kappa>0\) and \(\sigma_{r+1}=0\).  Therefore, whenever \(\|H\|_{\mathrm{op}}<\kappa/3\), the first \(r\) singular values remain separated from the rest: the variational characterization of singular values gives \(|\sigma_k(M+H)-\sigma_k(M)|\le\|H\|_{\mathrm{op}}\).  Hence the rank-\(r\) spectral projectors and the rank-\(r\) truncation are differentiable on this neighborhood.

Choose orthogonal complements \(U_\perp,V_\perp\) and write
\[
 U^\top H V=H_{11},\quad U^\top H V_\perp=H_{12},\quad
 U_\perp^\top H V=H_{21},\quad U_\perp^\top H V_\perp=H_{22}.
\]
Differentiating the equations defining the two separated singular subspaces shows that the tangent perturbation of the rank-\(r\) truncation retains the first three blocks and removes the normal block:
\[
 D(M\mapsto M_r)_M[H]
 =UH_{11}V^\top+UH_{12}V_\perp^\top+U_\perp H_{21}V^\top.
\]
This equation can also be checked directly: multiplying on the left and right by the four pairs of projectors \((UU^\top,I-UU^\top)\) and \((VV^\top,I-VV^\top)\) gives respectively \(H_{11},H_{12},H_{21},0\), which are exactly the first-order blocks selected by the separated spectral projector.

Since \(P=M^+=V\Sigma^{-1}U^\top\), inversion of the perturbed nonzero singular block and differentiation of the two singular subspaces give
\[
 D(M_r^+)_M[H]
 =-V\Sigma^{-1}H_{11}\Sigma^{-1}U^\top
 +V\Sigma^{-2}H_{21}^\top U_\perp^\top
 +V_\perp H_{12}^\top\Sigma^{-2}U^\top.
\]
Every term is linear in \(H\).  Now \(MP=UU^\top\), \(PM=VV^\top\), \(PP^\top=V\Sigma^{-2}V^\top\), and \(P^\top P=U\Sigma^{-2}U^\top\).  Substitution into the preceding display gives, term by term,
\[
 D(M_r^+)_M[H]
 =-PHP+PP^\top H^\top(I-MP)+(I-PM)H^\top P^\top P
 =\mathcal L_M(H).
\]
The discarded block \(H_{22}\) contributes zero, so this formula holds for arbitrary ambient perturbations, not merely tangent perturbations of fixed-rank matrices.  Finally, ordinary addition and multiplication of finite matrices are bilinear, whence the product rule applied to \(\mathcal F(y,M,B)=yM_r^+B\) yields
\[
 D\mathcal F_{(y,M,B)}[h_y,H,h_B]
 =h_yPB+y\mathcal L_M(H)B+yPh_B.
\]
This is a Fr\'echet derivative because the spectral projectors, inversion of the nonzero \(r\times r\) block, and matrix multiplication all have remainders that are quadratic uniformly on a smaller gap neighborhood.  The displayed formula includes the perturbations of all three learned blocks and both projector corrections, as claimed.

proposed_assumptions.condition:
For every \(c\in\mathcal C\), fold \(f\), and coordinate \(\ell\), conditional on the training sample, the signed Stieltjes measure
\[
 d\mathcal R_{cf}(u\mid X_{ci})
 :=d\left\{\frac{Q_c(u\mid X_{ci})}{\widehat Q_{c,-f}(u\mid X_{ci})}-1\right\},
 \qquad 0<u\le t_{c\ell},
\]
with the product-integral \(0/0=1\) convention, satisfies
\[
 \max_{c,f,\ell}
 \left\|
   \left|d\mathcal R_{cf}(\cdot\mid X_{ci})\right|((0,t_{c\ell}])
 \right\|_{L_2(P_c)}=O_P(a_K).
\]
Here \(\lvert d\mathcal R_{cf}\rvert\) denotes total variation of the signed measure.
proposed_assumptions.reason: The exact Duhamel remainder integrates the censor error against a signed relative-survival measure. Westling's B1(c) supremum ratio metric does not control the total variation of that measure, so the frozen product-rate premise alone does not yield \(O_P(a_Kb_K)\).
proposed_assumptions.standard_or_novel: novel: a total-variation strengthening of event-nuisance convergence that rules out increasingly oscillatory fitted hazards while retaining nonparametric survival learners
proposed_assumptions.not_crux: This condition is a primitive norm-rate restriction on a nuisance learner. It does not assert orthogonality, an asymptotic expansion, or a remainder bound; those conclusions follow from the displayed Duhamel identity and Cauchy--Schwarz.

proposed_assumptions.condition: For every \(c\in\mathcal C\), \(P_c(T_{ci}>0\mid X_{ci})=1\) almost surely.
proposed_assumptions.reason: Definition~\ref{def:aipcw-score} integrates over \((0,t]\) while its event indicator includes \(U=0\). Excluding a true event atom at the origin removes the corresponding population boundary discrepancy.
proposed_assumptions.standard_or_novel: standard: the usual survival-analysis support convention that follow-up begins before any event can occur
proposed_assumptions.not_crux: This is only a time-origin support convention; it neither controls nuisance rates nor asserts any part of the desired asymptotic expansion.

proposed_assumptions.condition: For every \(c\in\mathcal C\) and fold \(f\), the event-survival learner satisfies \(\widehat Q_{c,-f}(0\mid X_{ci})=1\) almost surely.
proposed_assumptions.reason: The same open-left integral requires the fitted product-integral survival to start at one; otherwise its Duhamel identity has an unaccounted boundary term at zero.
proposed_assumptions.standard_or_novel: standard: normalization of a fitted survival curve at the start of follow-up
proposed_assumptions.not_crux: This is a deterministic normalization of the learner and does not assert orthogonality, convergence, or a remainder rate.

open_obligations.what_is_open: The claimed \(O_P(a_Kb_K)\) conditional remainder is false under the frozen B1(b)/B1(c) metrics; it closes after the proposed relative-survival total-variation rate, origin-support, and learner-normalization conditions are applied.
open_obligations.obstruction: Smooth hazards with amplitude \(\varepsilon_K\) and frequency \(\varepsilon_K^{-1}\) have B1(b) and B1(c) errors \(O(\varepsilon_K)\) but an AIPCW conditional bias of order \(\varepsilon_K\), not \(\varepsilon_K^2\). Taking \(\varepsilon_K=K^{-1/3}\) satisfies the frozen product rate while violating root-\(K\) asymptotic linearity.
open_obligations.attempted: The score mean was derived directly from the event counting-process and at-risk expectations, then reduced by the product-integral Duhamel identity. Integration by parts and the backward equation suffice for score \(L_2\) consistency, but neither converts B1(c) supremum convergence into total-variation convergence; the explicit oscillatory-hazard path certifies that this route cannot close from the frozen primitives.
open_obligations.partial_result:
The frozen conditions do prove the algebraic orthogonality identity but do not imply its advertised \(O_P(a_Kb_K)\) bound.  Fix a cell and coordinate, suppress their subscripts, and put \(t=t_{c\ell}\).  For \(N(u)=\mathbf 1\{U\le u,\Delta=1\}\) and \(Y(u)=\mathbf 1\{U\ge u\}\), conditional independent censoring and the event-before-censor convention give
\[
 E\{dN(u)\mid X\}=Q(u-\mid X)G(u\mid X)\Lambda(du\mid X),
 \qquad
 E\{Y(u)\mid X\}=Q(u-\mid X)G(u\mid X).
\]
For generic survival functions \(\bar Q,\bar G\), with \(\bar\Lambda\) the product-integral hazard of \(\bar Q\), conditional expectation of Definition~\ref{def:aipcw-score} is therefore
\[
 E\{\psi_t(O;\bar Q,\bar G)\mid X\}
 =\bar Q(t\mid X)\left[
 1+\int_{(0,t]}
 \frac{Q(u-\mid X)G(u\mid X)}{\bar Q(u\mid X)\bar G(u\mid X)}
 (\bar\Lambda-\Lambda)(du\mid X)
 \right].
\]
The product rule for product integrals gives the Duhamel identity
\[
 Q(t\mid X)
 =\bar Q(t\mid X)\left[
 1+\int_{(0,t]}
 \frac{Q(u-\mid X)}{\bar Q(u\mid X)}
 (\bar\Lambda-\Lambda)(du\mid X)
 \right].
\]
Indeed, at a jump \(u\), division by the post-jump value \(\bar Q(u\mid X)\) changes the ratio \(Q/\bar Q\) by exactly \(Q(u-)(\Delta\bar\Lambda-\Delta\Lambda)/\bar Q(u)\), and on the continuous part the ordinary product rule gives the same equality; summing the jump and continuous increments from zero to \(t\) proves the display.  Subtraction yields the exact conditional remainder
\[
 \mathfrak R_t(\bar Q,\bar G)
 =\bar Q(t\mid X)\int_{(0,t]}
 \left\{\frac{G(u\mid X)}{\bar G(u\mid X)}-1\right\}
 d\left\{\frac{Q(u\mid X)}{\bar Q(u\mid X)}-1\right\}.
\]
Thus neither nuisance contributes a first-order term.  Nevertheless, the B1(c) metric controls only a supremum norm of survival ratios and does not control the total variation of the last signed measure.

This is not a technical possibility only.  On \([0,1]\), take no covariates, let the true event and censor cumulative hazards both be \(u\), and let \(\varepsilon_K=K^{-1/3}\).  Use the deterministic nuisance sequences
\[
 \widehat\Lambda_Q(u)=u+\varepsilon_K\{1-\cos(u/\varepsilon_K)\},
 \qquad
 \widehat\Lambda_G(u)=u+\varepsilon_K\sin(u/\varepsilon_K).
\]
Their hazard densities are \(1+\sin(u/\varepsilon_K)\) and \(1+\cos(u/\varepsilon_K)\), hence are nonnegative.  Their survival functions are valid, uniformly positive on \([0,1]\), and satisfy both the B1(b) inverse-censor metric and the B1(c) event-ratio metric at rate \(O(\varepsilon_K)\).  Conditional independence holds by generating the two times independently, and the true score is bounded, so all frozen moment and positivity conditions hold.  At \(t=1\), however, the exact remainder is
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \mathfrak R_1
 &=\widehat Q(1)\int_0^1
 \{e^{\varepsilon_K\sin(u/\varepsilon_K)}-1\}
 e^{\varepsilon_K\{1-\cos(u/\varepsilon_K)\}}
 \sin(u/\varepsilon_K)\,du\\
 &=\frac{e^{-1}}{2}\varepsilon_K+O(\varepsilon_K^2).
 \end{aligned}
\]
The last equality follows from the uniform Taylor expansion of the exponentials and
\(\int_0^1\sin^2(u/\varepsilon_K)\,du=1/2+O(\varepsilon_K)\).  Hence \(a_Kb_K=O(K^{-2/3})=o(K^{-1/2})\), while \(\mathfrak R_1\asymp K^{-1/3}\).  This explicitly refutes the frozen remainder claim.

The proposed total-variation condition repairs exactly this gap.  With \(A_{cf}(X)=\sup_{u\le t}|1/\widehat G_{c,-f}(u\mid X)-1/G_c(u\mid X)|\) and \(V_{cf}(X)=|d\mathcal R_{cf}|((0,t])\), the exact identity and \(0\le\widehat Q\le1\), \(0\le G\le1\) give
\[
 |E\{\mathfrak R_t\mid\text{training}\}|
 \le E\{A_{cf}(X)V_{cf}(X)\mid\text{training}\}
 \le \|A_{cf}\|_2\|V_{cf}\|_2
 =O_P(a_Kb_K).
\]
The origin-support condition removes the otherwise omitted atom at zero from the integrals in Definition~\ref{def:aipcw-score}.  Finally, the B1(b) and B1(c) convergence metrics, the backward product-integral identity
\[
 \int_{(0,t\wedge U]}\frac{\bar Q(t\mid X)}{\bar Q(u\mid X)}\bar\Lambda(du\mid X)
 =1-\frac{\bar Q(t\mid X)}{\bar Q(t\wedge U\mid X)},
\]
and \(G\ge g\) imply
\(\|\psi_t(\widehat Q,\widehat G)-\psi_t(Q,G)\|_{L_2(P_c)}=O_P(a_K+b_K)=o_P(1)\).  Conditional Chebyshev applied fold by fold then makes the cross-fitted empirical term \(o_P(K^{-1/2})\).  The exact decomposition
\[
 \widehat s_{c\ell}-S_c(t)
 =K^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^K\phi_{c\ell}(O_{ci})
 +\sum_{f=1}^L\frac{|\mathcal V_{cf}|}{K}
 (\mathbb P_{cf}-P_c)\{\widehat\psi_{cf\ell}-\psi_{c\ell}\}
 +\sum_{f=1}^L\frac{|\mathcal V_{cf}|}{K}
 P_c\{\widehat\psi_{cf\ell}-\psi_{c\ell}\}
\]
therefore has respectively the asserted influence term, an \(o_P(K^{-1/2})\) empirical term, and an \(O_P(a_Kb_K)=o_P(K^{-1/2})\) bias term.  Finiteness of \(L\), \(\mathcal C\), and every \(d_c\) makes these conclusions joint by a finite union bound, and the same \(L_2\) estimate plus consistency of \(\widehat s_c\) gives \(L_2(P_c)\)-consistency of the centered plug-in influences.  Thus the target closes after, but not before, the three proposed primitive conditions are applied.

open_obligations.what_is_open: The spectral delta-method, Gaussian limit, plug-in influence consistency, covariance consistency, and causal-target argument are complete conditional on Lemma~\ref{lem:joint-cell-expansion}; that dependency cannot be declared proved before the proposed nuisance conditions are adjudicated.
open_obligations.obstruction: This theorem's leading expansion uses the cell lemma directly. Under the current frozen class the oscillatory-hazard witness gives a first-stage bias larger than \(K^{-1/2}\), which is transported by the spectral derivative and invalidates the asserted centered Gaussian law.
open_obligations.attempted: The rank-gap neighborhood, full three-block Fr\'echet expansion, Cram\'er--Wold characteristic-function calculation, plug-in \(L_2\) bound, covariance law of large numbers, and post-transport identification step were all derived. No additional obstruction remains after the cell lemma is repaired.
open_obligations.partial_result:
Stack the fixed collection of cell coordinates in a vector \(Z=(y,M,B,s_1)\), with matrices vectorized in the fixed row-donor order, and let \(\widehat Z\) be its estimated counterpart.  Lemma~\ref{lem:joint-cell-expansion}, Assumption~\ref{ass:fixed-panel}, and cross-cell independence give
\[
 \widehat Z-Z=K^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^K\Phi_i+o_P(K^{-1/2}),
 \qquad \|\widehat Z-Z\|_2=O_P(K^{-1/2}).
\]
Assumptions~\ref{ass:exact-rank} and~\ref{ass:singular-gap}, together with the singular-value inequality used in Lemma~\ref{lem:full-spectral-differential}, imply
\[
 \Pr\{\sigma_r(\widehat M)>\kappa/2, \sigma_{r+1}(\widehat M)<\kappa/2\}\longrightarrow1.
\]
On this event the rank-\(r\) map is in the differentiability neighborhood.  Lemma~\ref{lem:full-spectral-differential} and the finite-dimensional Fr\'echet expansion therefore give
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \widehat\theta-\theta
 &= (\widehat y-y)PB
 +y\mathcal L_M(\widehat M-M)B
 +yP(\widehat B-B)+o_P(K^{-1/2})\\
 &=K^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^K
 \{\Phi_{y,i}PB+y\mathcal L_M(\Phi_{M,i})B+yP\Phi_{B,i}\}
 +o_P(K^{-1/2})\\
 &=K^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^K\Phi_{\theta,i}+o_P(K^{-1/2}).
 \end{aligned}
\]
The factual block has directly
\(\widehat s_1-s_1=K^{-1}\sum_i\Phi_{1,i}+o_P(K^{-1/2})\).  Stacking these two identities proves the asserted asymptotic linear representation with \(\Phi_{\eta,i}\) from Definition~\ref{def:transported-influence}.

Each \(\Phi_i\) is centered by the definition of \(\phi_c\).  The vectors are independent and identically distributed over \(i\): within each cell this is Assumption~\ref{ass:cell-iid}, and the cell blocks are mutually independent by Assumption~\ref{ass:cross-cell-independence}.  Because the panel dimension and the derivative matrix are fixed, Assumption~\ref{ass:influence-moment} implies \(E\|\Phi_{\eta,i}\|_2^{2+\nu}<\infty\).  For any fixed \(a\in\mathbb R^{2J}\), expansion of the characteristic function at zero, with the \((2+\nu)\)-moment controlling the remainder, gives
\[
 \left[E\exp\{\mathrm i a^\top\Phi_{\eta,i}/\sqrt K\}\right]^K
 \longrightarrow \exp\{-a^\top\Omega_\eta a/2\}.
\]
Thus every scalar projection converges to the corresponding centered normal law, and the finite-dimensional Cram\'er--Wold argument yields
\[
 K^{-1/2}\sum_{i=1}^K\Phi_{\eta,i}\rightsquigarrow
 \mathcal N_{2J}(0,\Omega_\eta).
\]
Assumption~\ref{ass:nondegenerate-covariance} makes this normal law nondegenerate.

It remains to verify the plug-in assertions.  Lemma~\ref{lem:joint-cell-expansion} gives foldwise \(L_2\)-consistency of the cell influence blocks.  The first display gives \(\widehat y\to_Py\), \(\widehat M\to_PM\), and \(\widehat B\to_PB\).  Continuity of \(M\mapsto M_r^+\) and of its derivative on the gap neighborhood then implies, by a finite number of triangle and Cauchy--Schwarz inequalities,
\[
 K^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^K
 \|\widehat\Phi_{\eta,i}-\Phi_{\eta,i}\|_2^2=o_P(1).
\]
Indeed, terms containing a fitted cell influence difference are controlled by its conditional \(L_2\) norm, and terms containing an estimated spectral coefficient difference are its \(o_P(1)\) norm times the \(O_P(1)\) empirical second moment of the true influence.  Consequently,
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \|\widehat\Omega_\eta-K^{-1}\sum_i\Phi_{\eta,i}\Phi_{\eta,i}^\top\|_{\mathrm{op}}
 &\le
 \left\{K^{-1}\sum_i\|\widehat\Phi_{\eta,i}-\Phi_{\eta,i}\|_2^2\right\}^{1/2}\\
 &\quad\times
 \left[\left\{K^{-1}\sum_i\|\widehat\Phi_{\eta,i}\|_2^2\right\}^{1/2}
 +\left\{K^{-1}\sum_i\|\Phi_{\eta,i}\|_2^2\right\}^{1/2}\right]
 =o_P(1).
 \end{aligned}
\]
The ordinary finite-dimensional law of large numbers makes the remaining empirical second moment converge to \(\Omega_\eta\), proving \(\widehat\Omega_\eta\to_P\Omega_\eta\).

Finally, Assumption~\ref{ass:post-transport} equates \(yM_r^+B=\theta\) to the target unit's untreated post-treatment survival row; Assumption~\ref{ass:target-pre-span} supplies the exact donor representation.  Conditional censoring and positivity enter through Lemma~\ref{lem:joint-cell-expansion}, which estimates each marginal \(S_c(t)\).  Hence the limit concerns the causal transported curve and not a marginal Kaplan--Meier pseudo-target.

open_obligations.what_is_open: The multiplier band and studentized grid-RMST proof is complete conditional on Theorem~\ref{thm:joint-spectral-limit}, but that theorem remains open solely through the false frozen first-stage premise.
open_obligations.obstruction: Without centered joint root-\(K\) asymptotic linearity, neither the sampling maximum nor the scalar RMST statistic has the Gaussian limit used by the conditional multiplier and studentization arguments.
open_obligations.attempted: Conditional Gaussianity of the multipliers, positive definiteness of the counterfactual covariance block, continuity of the maximum law, quantile convergence, RMST variance positivity, and plug-in variance consistency were derived in full.
open_obligations.partial_result:
Let \(\Omega_\theta\) and \(\widehat\Omega_\theta\) denote the counterfactual \(J\times J\) principal blocks of \(\Omega_\eta\) and \(\widehat\Omega_\eta\).  Theorem~\ref{thm:joint-spectral-limit} gives \(\widehat\Omega_\theta\to_P\Omega_\theta\).  Assumption~\ref{ass:nondegenerate-covariance} implies
\[
 \lambda_{\min}(\Omega_\theta)\ge v,
 \qquad \sigma_j^2:=(\Omega_\theta)_{jj}\ge v,
 \qquad \widehat\sigma_j\to_P\sigma_j
\]
for every \(j\), because a principal submatrix cannot have a smaller Rayleigh quotient than the full matrix on its coordinate subspace.

Conditionally on the data, the multiplier vector
\[
 Z_K^*=K^{-1/2}\sum_{i=1}^K\xi_i\widehat\Phi_{\theta,i}
\]
is exactly Gaussian with mean zero and covariance \(\widehat\Omega_\theta\).  Therefore its studentized covariance converges in probability to
\(R=\operatorname{diag}(\Omega_\theta)^{-1/2}\Omega_\theta
\operatorname{diag}(\Omega_\theta)^{-1/2}\).  If \(Z\sim\mathcal N_J(0,R)\), then \(\max_j|Z_j|\) has a continuous distribution: \(R\) is positive definite, so \(Z\) has a density and the boundary of every cube has Lebesgue measure zero.  Continuity of Gaussian probabilities in a positive-definite covariance matrix consequently gives
\[
 c_{1-\alpha}^\star\to_P c_{1-\alpha},
 \qquad
 \Pr\{\max_j|Z_j|\le c_{1-\alpha}\}=1-\alpha.
\]
On the sampling side, Theorem~\ref{thm:joint-spectral-limit}, Slutsky's identity, and the same continuous mapping give
\[
 \max_{1\le j\le J}
 \left|\frac{\sqrt K(\widehat\theta_j-\theta_j)}{\widehat\sigma_j}\right|
 \rightsquigarrow \max_{1\le j\le J}|Z_j|.
\]
Combining the last two displays proves
\[
 \Pr\!\left\{\theta_j\in
 [\widehat\theta_j\pm c_{1-\alpha}^\star\widehat\sigma_j/\sqrt K]
 \text{ for all }1\le j\le J\right\}\longrightarrow1-\alpha.
\]
The fixedness of \(J\) in Assumption~\ref{ass:fixed-panel} is used here; no growing-grid Gaussian approximation is asserted.

For the scalar target, Definition~\ref{def:full-spectral-map} and Theorem~\ref{thm:joint-spectral-limit} give
\[
 \sqrt K(\widehat\tau_R-\tau_R)
 =K^{-1/2}\sum_{i=1}^K q^\top(\Phi_{1,i}-\Phi_{\theta,i})+o_P(1)
 =K^{-1/2}\sum_{i=1}^K\Phi_{\tau,i}+o_P(1).
\]
With \(a=(-q^\top,q^\top)^\top\in\mathbb R^{2J}\), its variance is
\[
 V_R=E\Phi_{\tau,i}^2=a^\top\Omega_\eta a
 \ge v\|a\|_2^2=2v\|q\|_2^2>0,
\]
where the last inequality uses that the prespecified \(q\) is nonzero.  The same empirical \(L_2\) argument used for \(\widehat\Omega_\eta\) shows
\[
 \widehat V_R=K^{-1}\sum_i
 \{q^\top(\widehat\Phi_{1,i}-\widehat\Phi_{\theta,i})\}^2
 \to_P V_R.
\]
The scalar characteristic-function calculation in the proof of Theorem~\ref{thm:joint-spectral-limit} and division by the consistent positive standard error now yield
\[
 \frac{\sqrt K(\widehat\tau_R-\tau_R)}{\sqrt{\widehat V_R}}
 \rightsquigarrow\mathcal N(0,1).
\]
Hence \(\widehat\tau_R\pm z_{1-\alpha/2}\sqrt{\widehat V_R/K}\) has limiting coverage \(1-\alpha\).  This is inference for the defined grid functional \(q^\top(s_1-\theta)\); no continuous-time RMST integral is introduced.

open_obligations.what_is_open: A conditional signal-to-noise frontier is proved, but the frozen core does not supply the repaired uniform triangular cell experiment needed to promote it to an unconditional resolution of the open-ended question.
open_obligations.obstruction: The handle relies on the same orthogonal cell experiment whose product-rate remainder is false as frozen. Uniform weak-gap coverage additionally requires a consistently estimable operator-noise scale and uniform standardized moment and covariance bounds along the triangular collection; none is presently a core premise.
open_obligations.attempted: Noise-threshold rank recovery, the relative Taylor remainder, exact Tikhonov bias, active-loading contiguous alternatives for both regular and rare-event noise scales, and the structurally inactive exception were derived without fixing a phase exponent.
open_obligations.partial_result:
In the fixed-dimensional orthogonal cell-score experiment, let \(\rho_K\) be a consistently estimable operator-norm noise scale satisfying \(\|\widehat M-M_K\|_{\mathrm{op}}=O_P(\rho_K)\), and suppose the larger nonzero singular values stay uniformly separated, the cell expansion and influence estimation are uniform over the collection under consideration, and the standardized first-stage covariance and \((2+\nu)\)-moments are uniformly nondegenerate and bounded.  Then the maximal unrestricted signal-to-noise region for ordinary shrinking-rank spectral inference is
\[
 \Delta_K/\rho_K\longrightarrow\infty.
\]
More precisely, for any \(h_K\to\infty\) with \(h_K\rho_K/\Delta_K\to0\), thresholding the singular values at \(h_K\widehat\rho_K\) selects rank \(r\) with probability tending to one uniformly, and the fully differentiated plug-in and multiplier construction gives a uniformly honest band for the unregularized curve \(y(M_K)_r^+B\).  Its \(j\)-th half-width has order \(\sigma_{Kj}/\sqrt K\), where \(\sigma_{Kj}^2=E\Phi_{\theta,i,j}^2\), and it shrinks precisely on subcollections for which \(\max_j\sigma_{Kj}/\sqrt K\to0\).

For the Tikhonov inverse \(P_{\lambda,K}=(M_K^\top M_K+\lambda_K^2I)^{-1}M_K^\top\), if \(M_K=\sum_{k=1}^r\sigma_{k,K}u_{k,K}v_{k,K}^\top\), its exact bias for the unregularized target is
\[
 yP_{\lambda,K}B-y(M_K)_r^+B
 =-\sum_{k=1}^r
 \frac{\lambda_K^2}{\sigma_{k,K}^2+\lambda_K^2}
 \frac{yv_{k,K}}{\sigma_{k,K}}u_{k,K}^\top B.
\]
Thus Tikhonov inference is honest for the unregularized curve only when this displayed bias is included in the band or is uniformly negligible relative to its standard error; regularization alone does not enlarge the unrestricted frontier.

The frontier cannot be characterized by \(\Delta_K\) alone on structurally restricted classes.  If the weak component \((yv_{r,K}/\sigma_{r,K})u_{r,K}^\top B\) vanishes identically on a known subclass, deleting that component yields the same target and rank-\((r-1)\) inference remains regular even when \(\Delta_K/\rho_K\) is bounded.  Conversely, on every unrestricted class allowing a nonzero weak component and local perturbations of its singular value, there are mutually contiguous two-path alternatives with \(\Delta_K\asymp\rho_K\) and a fixed separation of \(y(M_K)_r^+B\).  Hence no uniformly consistent estimator and, for any fixed \(0<\alpha<1/2\), no uniformly \((1-\alpha)\)-honest band with diameter converging to zero can exist on that remaining class.  Nonshrinking honest bands are not ruled out; the trivial survival range already supplies one.
\par\medskip\noindent\emph{Proof of the conditional partial result.}
Write \(E_K=\widehat M-M_K\).  The variational formula for singular values implies
\[
 |\sigma_j(\widehat M)-\sigma_j(M_K)|\le\|E_K\|_{\mathrm{op}}.
\]
If \(\widehat\rho_K/\rho_K\to_P1\), \(h_K\to\infty\), and \(h_K\rho_K/\Delta_K\to0\), then with probability tending to one every noise singular value below rank \(r\) is smaller than \(h_K\widehat\rho_K\), while
\[
 \sigma_r(\widehat M)
 \ge\Delta_K-\|E_K\|_{\mathrm{op}}
 >h_K\widehat\rho_K.
\]
The separated larger singular values are also retained.  Thus \(\Pr(\widehat r=r)\to1\), uniformly whenever the displayed stochastic bounds and signal-to-noise divergence are uniform.

On the event \(\|E_K\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le\Delta_K/2\), singular-coordinate inversion is analytic.  In the singular bases, every first derivative contains at most two inverse singular factors, while differentiating it once more adds at most one factor \(\Delta_K^{-1}\).  For a counterfactual coordinate whose gradient is \(D_{Kj}\), the uniform covariance lower bound makes its standard deviation comparable to \(\|D_{Kj}\|_2\), and the second-order Taylor remainder obeys
\[
 |R_{Kj}|
 \le C\|D_{Kj}\|_2\Delta_K^{-1}\|\widehat Z-Z\|_2^2.
\]
Since \(\|\widehat Z-Z\|_2=O_P(\rho_K)\), its ratio to the linear standard error is \(O_P(\rho_K/\Delta_K)=o_P(1)\).  The same calculation shows that replacing \(D_{Kj}\) by its plug-in version changes the standardized influence by \(o_P(1)\).  The fixed-dimensional characteristic-function argument is uniform under the stipulated standardized \((2+\nu)\)-moment bound, and, conditionally on the data, Gaussian multipliers are exactly Gaussian with the plug-in covariance.  Repeating the cube-boundary argument from Theorem~\ref{thm:band-and-rmst} proves uniform coverage.  The stated half-width and its shrinking criterion follow directly from studentization.

For Tikhonov regularization, substitute the singular-value formulas
\[
 P_{\lambda,K}=\sum_{k=1}^r
 \frac{\sigma_{k,K}}{\sigma_{k,K}^2+\lambda_K^2}v_{k,K}u_{k,K}^\top,
 \qquad
 (M_K)_r^+=\sum_{k=1}^r\sigma_{k,K}^{-1}v_{k,K}u_{k,K}^\top.
\]
Termwise subtraction gives the exact bias formula in the statement.  Since its weak summand can be a fixed nonzero vector when \(\sigma_{r,K}\) is at the noise scale, it cannot be called negligible without an explicit loading restriction or an honest bias radius.

We next give the promised two-path certificate.  For \(r\ge2\), embed the following \(2\times2\) block in the last two singular directions and keep all earlier singular directions fixed and separated.  Let \(u_1=(1,1)^\top/\sqrt2\), \(u_2=(1,-1)^\top/\sqrt2\), \(v_1=(2,1)^\top/\sqrt5\), and \(v_2=(1,-2)^\top/\sqrt5\).  Choose fixed interior constants \(\sigma_1,y_0,b_0,a,b>0\), small enough that every coordinate below is in \((0,1)\) and each two-time survival row is strictly decreasing.  Put
\[
 M_K^{(0)}=\sigma_1u_1v_1^\top+\frac{c}{\sqrt K}u_2v_2^\top,
 \quad y_K=y_0v_1^\top+\frac{ac}{\sqrt K}v_2^\top,
 \quad B=b_0u_1+bu_2,
\]
and replace \(c/\sqrt K\) by \((c+h)/\sqrt K\) in \(M_K^{(1)}\), leaving \(y_K,B\) unchanged.  Strict interiority and strict time monotonicity at the rank-one limit persist for all large \(K\).  Each survival row is realized by a three-category event-time distribution over before the first time, between the two times, and after the second time; take \(C=\infty\), so conditional censoring and positivity hold.  The two observed laws differ only by \(O(K^{-1/2})\) in finitely many interior multinomial probabilities.  Taylor expansion of their log likelihood ratio gives
\[
 \log\frac{dP_K^{(1)}}{dP_K^{(0)}}
 =h\,Z_K-\frac{h^2}{2}I+o_{P_K^{(0)}}(1),
\]
where \(Z_K\rightsquigarrow\mathcal N(0,I)\) and \(0<I<\infty\); the reciprocal expansion holds under \(P_K^{(1)}\).  Hence the paths are mutually contiguous.  Their weak target components are
\[
 ab
 \quad\text{and}\quad
 ab\frac{c}{c+h},
\]
whose separation \(abh/(c+h)\) is fixed and nonzero.

For \(r=1\), the same certificate uses one pre coordinate with \(M_K^{(0)}=c/K\), \(M_K^{(1)}=(c+h)/K\), \(y_K=ac/K\), and \(B=b\).  The donor-pre event counts converge respectively to Poisson laws of means \(c\) and \(c+h\), which are mutually absolutely continuous; their likelihood-ratio sequences are therefore mutually contiguous, while the same two target values \(ab\) and \(abc/(c+h)\) result.  Here the observable rare-event noise scale is \(K^{-1}\), so again \(\Delta_K\asymp\rho_K\).

To convert contiguity into the band obstruction, fix \(0<\alpha<1/2\) and choose \(h>0\) sufficiently small that the limiting total-variation distance of the two experiments is less than \(1-2\alpha\).  If a band covered each path with probability at least \(1-\alpha+o(1)\), transfer of the second coverage event to the first law and the union bound would give positive limiting probability that the band contains both separated target values.  Its diameter therefore cannot converge to zero.  A uniformly consistent estimator would yield a test separating the two paths and is ruled out by the same likelihood-ratio argument.

Finally, if \((yv_{r,K}/\sigma_{r,K})u_{r,K}^\top B=0\) identically on a known subclass, then the rank-\(r\) and rank-\((r-1)\) transported targets are equal term by term in the singular expansion.  Since the \((r-1)\)-st singular value remains separated, the fixed-gap proof applies after dropping the weak component.  This establishes both the structural exception and the conclusion that the maximal unrestricted frontier is signal-to-noise, not a phase exponent depending only on \(K\).

proofs.proof_tex:
We first establish the probability limit and the continuity assertion.  For a cell \(c\) and a time \(u\) in a fixed finite support, define the empirical event submass and empirical risk probability by
\[
 \widehat d_{cK}(u)=\frac1K\sum_{i=1}^K
       \mathbf 1\{U_{ci}=u,\Delta_{ci}=1\},\qquad
 \widehat R_{cK}(u)=\frac1K\sum_{i=1}^K
       \mathbf 1\{U_{ci}\ge u\},
\]
and let \(d_c(u)\) and \(R_c(u)\) denote their expectations under \(P_c\).  By the within-cell i.i.d. sampling assumption, each summand is Bernoulli and hence
\[
 \operatorname{Var}\{\widehat d_{cK}(u)\}\le \frac{1}{4K},
 \qquad
 \operatorname{Var}\{\widehat R_{cK}(u)\}\le \frac{1}{4K}.
\]
Consequently, for every \(\varepsilon>0\), Chebyshev's inequality, obtained by applying Markov's inequality to the squared centered mean, gives
\[
 P_c\!\left(\left|\widehat d_{cK}(u)-d_c(u)\right|>\varepsilon\right)
 \le \frac{1}{4K\varepsilon^2},\qquad
 P_c\!\left(\left|\widehat R_{cK}(u)-R_c(u)\right|>\varepsilon\right)
 \le \frac{1}{4K\varepsilon^2}.
\]
The fixed-panel assumption makes the total number of cells and retained coordinates finite.  A finite union bound therefore yields joint convergence of all these empirical submasses and risk probabilities.  Wherever \(R_c(u)>0\), division is continuous, and thus the empirical Kaplan--Meier product satisfies
\[
 \widehat S^{\mathrm{KM}}_{cK}(t_{c\ell})
 =\prod_{u\le t_{c\ell}}
   \left\{1-\frac{\widehat d_{cK}(u)}{\widehat R_{cK}(u)}\right\}
 \ \xrightarrow{p}\ 
 \prod_{u\le t_{c\ell}}
   \left\{1-\frac{d_c(u)}{R_c(u)}\right\}
 =\widetilde S_c(t_{c\ell}).
\]
This directly verifies, rather than assumes, the cellwise probability-limit assertion on the finite discrete submodel.  In the general product-integral version of the definition, \(\widetilde S_c\) is precisely the corresponding cellwise marginal Kaplan--Meier probability limit; the remainder of this argument only uses convergence at the fixed retained coordinates.  Extracting blocks is linear, so the fixed number of coordinatewise limits gives
\[
 (\widehat y^{\mathrm{KM}},\widehat M^{\mathrm{KM}},
   \widehat B^{\mathrm{KM}})
 \xrightarrow{p}(\widetilde y,\widetilde M,\widetilde B).
\]

For completeness, we verify the needed spectral continuity.  Let \(A_n\to A\) in operator norm and suppose
\[
 \sigma_r(A)>\sigma_{r+1}(A),
\]
where a missing singular value is interpreted as zero.  The variational characterization of singular values and the triangle inequality give, directly,
\[
 |\sigma_k(A_n)-\sigma_k(A)|\le \|A_n-A\|_{\mathrm{op}}
\]
for every \(k\).  Let \(\Pi_n\) be the orthogonal projector onto the leading \(r\) right singular subspace of \(A_n\).  The set of rank-\(r\) orthogonal projectors is compact.  Every convergent subsequence of \((\Pi_n)\) has a limit maximizing
\[
 Q\longmapsto \operatorname{tr}(Q A^\top A)
\]
over rank-\(r\) orthogonal projectors, because \(\Pi_n\) maximizes the analogous criterion with \(A_n^\top A_n\).  The displayed strict singular gap makes this maximizer unique: it is the projector \(\Pi\) onto the leading \(r\) right singular subspace of \(A\).  Thus every convergent subsequence has limit \(\Pi\), and compactness implies \(\Pi_n\to\Pi\).  It follows that
\[
 (A_n)_r=A_n\Pi_n\longrightarrow A\Pi=A_r.
\]
Moreover, \(\sigma_r(A)>0\), so for all sufficiently large \(n\) the matrix
\[
 (A_n)_r^\top(A_n)_r+I-\Pi_n
\]
is invertible.  A singular-value decomposition verifies the identity
\[
 (A_n)_r^+
 =\left\{(A_n)_r^\top(A_n)_r+I-\Pi_n\right\}^{-1}(A_n)_r^\top.
\]
Matrix inversion is continuous at an invertible matrix, and hence
\[
 (A_n)_r^+\longrightarrow A_r^+.
\]
Applying this fact at \(A=\widetilde M\), whose separated rank means the displayed strict gap, and then applying continuity of matrix multiplication proves
\[
 \widehat y^{\mathrm{KM}}
       (\widehat M^{\mathrm{KM}})_r^+
       \widehat B^{\mathrm{KM}}
 \xrightarrow{p}
 \widetilde y(\widetilde M)_r^+\widetilde B.
\]

Now parameterize the finite discrete submodel by its finitely many cell-atom probabilities.  Each true survival coordinate is a finite sum of event atom probabilities.  Each marginal Kaplan--Meier coordinate is a finite product of ratios of affine functions of the atom probabilities.  It is therefore continuous wherever every risk denominator is positive.  The preceding spectral argument shows that the two maps \(M\mapsto M_r^+\) and \(\widetilde M\mapsto(\widetilde M)_r^+\) are continuous wherever their rank-\(r\) singular gaps are positive.  Hence the discrepancy map
\[
 p\longmapsto
 \beta_{\mathrm{KM}}(p)
 =\widetilde y(p)(\widetilde M(p))_r^+\widetilde B(p)
  -y(p)(M(p))_r^+B(p)
\]
is continuous on that domain.  If \(\mathcal S\) denotes the finite-support conditional-censoring, positivity, exact-rank, and exact-transport submodel, then
\[
 \mathcal U=
 \left\{p\in\mathcal S:
   \begin{array}{l}
   \text{all required risks are positive, the true and naive rank-\(r\)}\\[-2pt]
   \text{singular gaps are positive, and }\|\beta_{\mathrm{KM}}(p)\|_2>0
   \end{array}
 \right\}
\]
is the intersection of \(\mathcal S\) with an open set in the ambient finite-dimensional probability simplex.  Thus \(\mathcal U\) is relatively open in \(\mathcal S\).  This is the asserted open subclass on which the well-defined unadjusted PCR probability limit differs from the transported causal curve \(\theta=yM_r^+B\); the equality with that causal curve uses the exact post-transport assumption and is not part of the definition of the naive functional.

It remains to verify that the stated witness belongs to \(\mathcal U\).  Its six displayed true survival pairs, with the repeated factual-post pair retained, are
\[
 (a,b)\in
 \left\{(7/10,9/20),(4/5,3/5),(3/5,3/10),
 (7/10,2/5),(1/2,1/5),(7/10,2/5)\right\}.
\]
For \(\epsilon_x=2x-1\), the three conditional event atom masses in the definition of \(P^\star\) obey, uniformly over this list and \(x\in\{0,1\}\),
\[
 1-a-\frac{\epsilon_x}{20}\ge\frac3{20},\qquad
 a-b+\frac{\epsilon_x}{40}\ge\frac7{40},\qquad
 b+\frac{\epsilon_x}{40}\ge\frac7{40}.
\]
They sum to one.  The three censor atom masses are, for \(x=0\),
\[
 (1-\gamma_{10},\gamma_{10}-\gamma_{20},\gamma_{20})
 =(1/5,3/10,1/2),
\]
and, for \(x=1\),
\[
 (1-\gamma_{11},\gamma_{11}-\gamma_{21},\gamma_{21})
 =(2/5,1/5,2/5).
\]
Thus every displayed atom mass is strictly positive.  Conditional independent censoring holds because the construction draws \(T_{ci}\) and \(C_{ci}\) independently conditional on \(X_{ci}\).  Also
\[
 P_c(T_{ci}>t_{c1}\mid X_{ci}=x)=a+\frac{\epsilon_x}{20},
 \qquad
 P_c(T_{ci}>t_{c2}\mid X_{ci}=x)=b+\frac{\epsilon_x}{40}.
\]
Since \(P_c(X_{ci}=0)=P_c(X_{ci}=1)=1/2\), averaging over \(X_{ci}\) gives the advertised marginal event-survival pair \((a,b)\).  Finally, for every \(0\le t\le t_{c2}\),
\[
 G_c(t\mid x)=P_c(C_{ci}\ge t\mid X_{ci}=x)
 \ge P_c(C_{ci}=\infty\mid X_{ci}=x)
 =\gamma_{2x}\ge\frac25,
\]
which proves censoring positivity on the required horizon.

We next calculate the marginal Kaplan--Meier functional under the event-wins-ties convention \(\Delta_{ci}=\mathbf 1\{T_{ci}\le C_{ci}\}\).  At the first time,
\[
 R_c(t_{c1})=P_c(U_{ci}\ge t_{c1})=1,
 \qquad
 d_c(t_{c1})=P_c(U_{ci}=t_{c1},\Delta_{ci}=1)=1-a.
\]
At the second time, conditional independence and the two covariate strata give
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 R_c(t_{c2})
 &=\frac12\left\{(a-1/20)\frac45+(a+1/20)\frac35\right\}\\
 &=\frac{140a-1}{200},
 \end{aligned}
\]
and
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 d_c(t_{c2})
 &=\frac12\left\{(a-b-1/40)\frac45
                   +(a-b+1/40)\frac35\right\}\\
 &=\frac{280(a-b)-1}{400}.
 \end{aligned}
\]
The smallest displayed value of \(a\) is \(1/2\), so
\[
 R_c(t_{c2})\ge\frac{140(1/2)-1}{200}=\frac{69}{200}>0.
\]
The first Kaplan--Meier factor is \(1-(1-a)=a\), and the second gives
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \widetilde S_c(t_{c2})
 &=a\left\{1-
   \frac{[280(a-b)-1]/400}{(140a-1)/200}\right\}\\
 &=a\left\{1-\frac{280(a-b)-1}{280a-2}\right\}
 =\frac{a(280b-1)}{280a-2}.
 \end{aligned}
\]
Therefore the marginal Kaplan--Meier pair is exactly
\[
 \left(a,\frac{a(280b-1)}{280a-2}\right).
\]
Substitution of the six pairs gives
\[
 \widetilde y=(7/10,175/388),\qquad
 \widetilde M=
 \begin{pmatrix}4/5&334/555\\3/5&3/10\end{pmatrix},\qquad
 \widetilde B=
 \begin{pmatrix}7/10&777/1940\\1/2&55/276\end{pmatrix}.
\]
The factual-post pair is the repeated pair \((7/10,2/5)\), so its naive limit is \((7/10,777/1940)\), and it is not an argument of the counterfactual map in the definition of \(\beta_{\mathrm{KM}}\).

For the true donor-pre matrix,
\[
 \det(M)=\frac45\frac3{10}-\frac35\frac35=-\frac3{25}\ne0.
\]
Thus \(\operatorname{rank}(M)=r=2\), its rank gap is positive, and its row space is all of \(\mathbb R^2\), so the target-pre-span condition holds.  Direct inversion gives
\[
 yM^{-1}=(1/2,1/2),\qquad
 yM^{-1}B=(1/2,1/2)
 \begin{pmatrix}7/10&2/5\\1/2&1/5\end{pmatrix}
 =(3/5,3/10).
\]
The witness assigns its latent untreated target-post row to this last vector, so the exact post-transport condition holds and \(\theta=(3/5,3/10)\).  For the naive donor-pre matrix,
\[
 \det(\widetilde M)
 =\frac45\frac3{10}-\frac35\frac{334}{555}
 =-\frac{112}{925}\ne0.
\]
Hence the naive rank-two gap is also positive and \((\widetilde M)_2^+=\widetilde M^{-1}\).  Exact elimination yields
\[
 \widetilde y\widetilde M^{-1}
 =\left(\frac{777}{1552},\frac{581}{1164}\right).
\]
Multiplying by \(\widetilde B\) coordinate by coordinate gives
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \widetilde y\widetilde M^{-1}\widetilde B
 &=\left(
 \frac{777}{1552}\frac7{10}+\frac{581}{1164}\frac12,
 \frac{777}{1552}\frac{777}{1940}
       +\frac{581}{1164}\frac{55}{276}
 \right)\\
 &=\left(\frac{27937}{46560},
          \frac{186964603}{623252160}\right)\\
 &=\left(\frac35+\frac1{46560},
          \frac3{10}-\frac{2209}{124650432}\right).
 \end{aligned}
\]
By the definition of \(\beta_{\mathrm{KM}}\),
\[
 \beta_{\mathrm{KM}}(P^\star)
 =\left(\frac1{46560},-\frac{2209}{124650432}\right)\ne(0,0).
\]
Thus \(P^\star\in\mathcal U\).  Continuity supplies a relative neighborhood of \(P^\star\) inside the stated conditional-censoring, positivity, exact-rank, exact-transport submodel on which this nonzero discrepancy persists.  Since the unadjusted estimator converges there to \(\theta+\beta_{\mathrm{KM}}\) rather than to the causal curve \(\theta\), the bias is fixed and does not vanish as \(K\to\infty\), completing the proof.

proposed.statement:
Whenever \(\widetilde M\) has separated rank \(r\), unadjusted cellwise Kaplan--Meier followed by rank-\(r\) PCR converges to \(\widetilde y(\widetilde M)_r^+\widetilde B\). On the finite discrete submodel with fixed supports and positive risk denominators, the map from cell-atom probabilities to \(\widetilde y(\widetilde M)_r^+\widetilde B-yM_r^+B\) is continuous wherever the true and naive singular gaps are positive. Consequently, the laws for which the unadjusted probability limit differs from \(\theta\) form a relatively open subset of the conditional-censoring, positivity, exact-rank, exact-transport submodel. For every pair \((a,b)\) in the six-cell construction \(P^\star\), the displayed event and censor atom masses are strictly positive. Under the event-wins-ties convention, the two marginal at-risk denominators are \(P_c(U_{ci}\ge t_{c1})=1\) and \(P_c(U_{ci}\ge t_{c2})=(140a-1)/200\ge69/200\), while \(G_c\) is at least \(2/5\) on the required horizon. Hence \(P^\star\) belongs to the full six-cell conditional-censoring, positivity, exact-rank, exact-transport submodel. Its marginal Kaplan--Meier limit for a cell with true pair \((a,b)\) is
\[
\left(a,\frac{a(280b-1)}{280a-2}\right),
\]
and therefore
\[
\widetilde y=(7/10,175/388),\quad \widetilde M=\begin{pmatrix}4/5&334/555\\3/5&3/10\end{pmatrix},\quad \widetilde B=\begin{pmatrix}7/10&777/1940\\1/2&55/276\end{pmatrix}.
\]
The target factual-post cell has the same displayed marginal pair as the first donor-post cell, so its marginal Kaplan--Meier limit is \((7/10,777/1940)\); this sixth curve does not enter the counterfactual PCR map. Since \(\det(M)=-3/25\), \(yM^{-1}=(1/2,1/2)\), and \(\theta=(3/5,3/10)\), direct substitution gives
\[
\widetilde y\widetilde M^{-1}\widetilde B=\left(27937/46560,186964603/623252160\right)=\left(3/5+1/46560,3/10-2209/124650432\right),
\]
so \(\beta_{\mathrm{KM}}=(1/46560,-2209/124650432)\ne(0,0)\).
proposed.justification: The proposition turns cellwise Kaplan--Meier distortion into an exact three-block PCR probability limit and shows that fixed bias persists under local perturbations of an explicit law.
proposed.gap: Curth et al. (2024) show survival-control distributional bias and Westling et al. (2024) explain Kaplan--Meier inconsistency, but neither derives the three-block PCR probability limit or a relatively open nonzero-bias subclass.
proposed.consumer: The result tells users of Han and Shah's workflow exactly when covariate-adjusted censoring is indispensable rather than a variance-only refinement.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The convergence clause uses the frozen within-cell i.i.d. sampling assumption for the empirical Kaplan--Meier law of large numbers and the frozen fixed-panel assumption for joint convergence over finitely many cells and coordinates. These two load-bearing dependencies were missing from the statement metadata; the claim itself is unchanged.
